newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH NUTRECO TO SEEK AMSTERDAM FLOTATION.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH NUTRECO TO SEEK AMSTERDAM FLOTATION.

text.p: Dutch animal and fish feeds group Nutreco Holding said on Monday it would seek a listing of its shares on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in connection with an initial public offering before the end of this summer.
"Nutreco considers the listing important to broaden its shareholder base, to provide access to the capital market for future growth and liquidity for the shares," the company said in a statement.
It added that Goldman Sachs International and Rabo Securities had been appointed as joint global coordinators of the initial public offering.

Nutreco emerged in 1994 from a management buy-out of British Petroleum's nutrition unit. In 1996 it privately placed cumulative preference shares with Dutch institutional investors, raising 150 million guilders to redeem long-term debt.

The company has leading positions in the feed and nutrition markets for livestock related agriculture and aquaculture. It is also active in the breeding and processing of poultry and pigs and in salmon farming.
Nutreco posted 1996 net profit of 40.4 million guilders, up more than 50 percent from 1995's 26.0 million. The company's 1996 turnover grew by 13 percent to 4.56 billion guilders.
Operating income increased by 13.3 percent to 128 million guilders last year.
Nutreco said it expected 1997 operating results to show a further improvement if current market conditions continued for the rest of this year.
